title: Rome’s sacrifice-only censure of Jeroboam clashes with her own per-accidens latria of divine images
source_text: XLII. Quod vero dicunt Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae, Jeroboam, etiamsi verum Deum in vitulis colere voluerit, nihilominus graviter peccasse, quod vitulis illis sacrificaverit, quoniam sacrificium soli Deo debetur, & inter externos latriae actus praecipuus est: hoc, inquam, non satis concordat cum ipsorum hypothesibus. Docent enim, ut thesibus praecedentibus probatum est, nihil prohibere quo minus imagines personae divinae latria colantur, id est, cultu summo qui Deo proprius est, modo id fiat non per se, sed per accidens: non absolute, sed relative: non primario, sed solum secundario, & concomitanter. Si semel autem conceditur, Israelitas in vitulis coluisse verum Deum, manifestum est totum illum cultum relativum fuisse, non autem absolutum: & vitulos non propter se sed propter Deum adoratos; nec primario, sed tantum concomitanter, & secundario. Jam vero, si Dei imagines caeteris Latriae actibus, tum internis, tum externis, ea ratione jam dictum est, Deo coadorari possunt, cur non quoque sacrificiis, & victimarum oblationibus, eodem modo coli potuerint? nimirum, aut improprie, aut per accidens, aut concomitanter, quomodo, & non aliter, ex eorum hypothesi, Israelitae vitulos coluerunt.
pass_a_gloss: But what the Doctors of the Roman Church say, that Jeroboam, even if he wished to cultivate the true God in the calves, nevertheless sinned gravely, because he sacrificed to those calves, since sacrifice is due to God alone, and is the chief among the exterior acts of latria: this, I say, does not sufficiently agree with their own hypotheses. For they teach, as was proved in the preceding theses, that nothing prohibits images of a divine person from being cultivated with latria, that is, with the highest cult which is proper to God, provided that be done not per se, but per accidents: not absolutely, but relatively: not primarily, but only secondarily, and concomitantly. But if once it is conceded that the Israelites cultivated the true God in the calves, it is manifest that that whole cult was relative, not absolute: and that the calves were adored not on account of themselves but on account of God; nor primarily, but only concomitantly, and secondarily. Now indeed, if the images of God can be co-adored to God by the remaining acts of Latria, both interior and exterior, by that reason already stated, why could they not also have been cultivated in the same mode by sacrifices and offerings of victims? namely, either improperly, or per accidents, or concomitantly, in which mode, and not otherwise, on their hypothesis, the Israelites cultivated the calves.
pass_b_english: Rome says Jeroboam’s fatal step was sacrifice—latria’s chief exterior act.
Yet she already allows per-accidens / relative / concomitant latria of God’s images in other acts—so why not in sacrifice on the same terms?
